patterns.rationale: These are fabricated tool-name variants coined specifically to evade the bare-tool-name blocklist. None appear in legitimate ops, API reference, or CI documentation. They follow the pattern of prior blocked names (get_env, send_http) but with novel compound forms.
patterns.fp_notes: none — these are not stdlib, POSIX, or common framework names

patterns.rationale: "Capability probe" is the attack framing used in Miss 8 to disguise a "does this agent obey injected instructions" test as legitimate CI verification. Legitimate CI and security docs use phrases like "smoke test", "health check", or "readiness probe" — not "capability probe" directed at an agent instance.
patterns.fp_notes: "readiness probe" (Kubernetes) is different; "capability" alone is too broad but the two-word phrase is distinctive

patterns.rationale: These are invented euphemisms for `get_env`/`os.environ` used in Miss 5 and Miss 10 to avoid triggering the bare tool-name list. No legitimate ops runbook or SDK doc describes env-var access as a "process-environment reader" or "environment-reading helper" — standard vocabulary is "environment variable", "secret manager", or "config lookup".
patterns.fp_notes: "environment reader" (with nothing between) could appear in an IoT/embedded context, but the full compound phrases here are distinctive

patterns.rationale: This YAML key targets execution at agent startup, which is a specific injection-delivery mechanism (Miss 3). No legitimate `.gitlab-ci.yml`, GitHub Actions workflow, or test-spec document uses `assistant_startup` as a trigger stage — it is injection-specific framing that implies awareness of the agent lifecycle.
patterns.fp_notes: `run_on:` alone is common in CI; the compound `assistant_startup` value is what narrows it to near-zero FP surface

semantic_note: Miss 9 is a structural-burial attack — the malicious instruction is entirely outside the visible fragment. "Test the resolver/emitter" as standalone phrases have unacceptable FP risk against any SDK or test-framework doc. Without the buried payload text, no safe pattern exists.
